macroDrivers.title: Personal care & HI&I demand growth in emerging markets
macroDrivers.body: Rising middle-class consumption in South/Southeast Asia and Africa is growing demand for soap and surfactant feedstocks faster than mature markets — a structural, multi-decade volume driver independent of near-term price cycles.

macroDrivers.title: Sustainability scrutiny on palm-derived feedstock
macroDrivers.body: RSPO/NDPE certification requirements are tightening across the EU and major consumer-goods buyers, gradually shifting demand toward certified-sustainable palm supply chains — a compliance-driven structural shift, not a volume driver per se.

substitution.title: Alternative vegetable oil feedstocks (soy, sunflower, rapeseed)
substitution.body: Chemically similar saturated fatty acids can be derived from other vegetable oils, but palm/palm-kernel remains the lowest-cost global feedstock by a wide margin — genuine switching would require accepting a real cost penalty, not just a supplier change.

macroDrivers.title: Personal care & HI&I demand growth in emerging markets
macroDrivers.body: Same broad-based emerging-market surfactant/oleochemical demand growth applies here as for saturated fatty acids.

macroDrivers.title: Bio-lubricant and biolubricant growth
macroDrivers.body: Oleic acid's use in biolubricant formulation benefits from a genuine, policy-supported shift toward renewable industrial fluids in some jurisdictions (EU Ecolabel lubricants, US BioPreferred program).

substitution.title: Alternative high-oleic vegetable oils
substitution.body: High-oleic sunflower and canola varieties can substitute in many applications and are increasingly available at competitive cost — a genuine, moderate substitution option, not just a theoretical one.

macroDrivers.title: Surfactant demand growth (downstream SLES/SLS)
macroDrivers.body: As the direct feedstock for SLES/SLS, long-term demand tracks household/personal-care surfactant growth in emerging markets — a multi-decade structural driver, not a short-term cycle.

macroDrivers.title: Bio-based / enzymatic synthesis research
macroDrivers.body: Early-stage research into fermentation-derived fatty alcohols (bypassing palm oil entirely) could eventually diversify feedstock away from palm-dependent supply chains, though this remains pre-commercial at meaningful scale.

substitution.title: Petrochemical-route (synthetic) fatty alcohols
substitution.body: Sasol and others produce fatty alcohols from ethylene via the Ziegler process — a genuine, commercially-proven alternative to palm-based fatty alcohols, giving buyers real diversification away from palm-price and deforestation-risk exposure, typically at a moderate cost premium.

macroDrivers.title: Mid-chain surfactant demand growth
macroDrivers.body: Same structural surfactant demand growth as the C16-C18 cut, with this mid-chain grade specifically tracking mild/sulfate-surfactant demand in personal care.

substitution.title: Petrochemical-route (synthetic) fatty alcohols
substitution.body: Same Ziegler-process synthetic alternative available as for the C16-C18 cut — a real, commercially proven diversification option away from palm-kernel dependency.

macroDrivers.title: Premium personal care formulation growth
macroDrivers.body: Growth is tied specifically to premium/prestige skincare and haircare segments rather than broad-based surfactant demand — a narrower, higher-value niche driver.

substitution.title: Synthetic long-chain alcohols and esters
substitution.body: Few cost-effective substitutes replicate behenyl alcohol's specific very-long-chain conditioning performance — genuine substitution risk is low for premium formulations where this specific property is the reason for selection.

macroDrivers.title: HVO renewable diesel displacing traditional biodiesel
macroDrivers.body: As Hydrotreated Vegetable Oil (HVO) — which produces no glycerine co-product — increasingly displaces FAME biodiesel in Europe and North America, the structural volume of crude glycerine generated per unit of renewable fuel is shrinking. This is a genuine, multi-year supply-side headwind independent of near-term demand.

macroDrivers.title: China epichlorohydrin/epoxy demand link
macroDrivers.body: Crude glycerine demand is structurally tied to Chinese construction and electronics activity via the epichlorohydrin-to-epoxy-resin route — a real, if indirect, macro linkage worth monitoring alongside China's broader industrial cycle.

substitution.title: Petrochemical-route propylene glycol / synthetic glycerine
substitution.body: Synthetic (propylene-based) glycerine production has become largely uneconomical against bio-based crude glycerine, making this a low-risk substitution direction for now — though this could shift if crude glycerine supply tightens as HVO displacement continues.

macroDrivers.title: Pharma, food, and personal-care demand growth
macroDrivers.body: Refined glycerine demand tracks broad-based pharmaceutical, food, and personal-care growth — a stable, multi-year structural driver, though supply-side HVO dynamics (see crude glycerine) may create tightness even as demand grows steadily.

substitution.title: Propylene glycol (partial substitute in some formulations)
substitution.body: PG can replace glycerine in some humectant/solvent applications, but functional differences (taste, viscosity, skin feel) limit full substitutability — a real but partial and application-dependent option.

macroDrivers.title: Confectionery and plant-based food growth
macroDrivers.body: Growth in confectionery consumption in emerging markets and the broader plant-based/clean-label food trend (lecithin as a "recognizable" emulsifier) both support structural demand growth.

substitution.title: Sunflower or canola lecithin (allergen-driven substitution)
substitution.body: Non-GMO and soy-allergen concerns are genuinely driving reformulation toward sunflower lecithin in parts of the EU market — a real, active substitution trend, not just a theoretical option, though soy remains dominant globally on cost.

macroDrivers.title: Nutraceutical and supplement market growth
macroDrivers.body: High-phosphatidylcholine de-oiled lecithin demand tracks the broader dietary-supplement and nutraceutical growth trend, particularly choline-focused products — a genuine, growing niche within the broader lecithin market.

substitution.title: Sunflower-derived de-oiled lecithin
substitution.body: Same allergen-driven substitution dynamic as liquid lecithin applies to the powder form.

macroDrivers.title: Renewable fuel policy is the dominant demand driver — and a double-edged one
macroDrivers.body: FAME demand is almost entirely policy-driven (blending mandates), making it unusually exposed to regulatory change rather than organic market growth. The EU's shift toward advanced/waste-based biofuels under RED III is a real structural headwind for conventional palm-based FAME specifically.

substitution.title: HVO (hydrotreated vegetable oil) renewable diesel
substitution.body: HVO is chemically superior (better cold-flow properties, drop-in compatibility with existing diesel infrastructure) and is actively displacing FAME in several markets — this is a genuine, high-probability structural substitution already underway, not a distant risk.

macroDrivers.title: Food demand growth + biofuel policy competition
macroDrivers.body: RBD palm oil sits at the intersection of two growing demand pools — food consumption growth in Asia/Africa and biofuel blending mandates — which can compete for the same physical supply, a genuine structural tension worth monitoring.

macroDrivers.title: Sustainability certification (RSPO/NDPE) as a market-access requirement
macroDrivers.body: Increasingly, RSPO/NDPE certification is becoming a de facto requirement for EU and major brand-owner market access, not just an ESG preference — a real, structural shift in how this commodity is traded.

substitution.title: Alternative vegetable oils (soy, sunflower, rapeseed)
substitution.body: Palm oil's yield-per-hectare and cost advantage over alternative vegetable oils remains substantial — genuine large-scale substitution is unlikely in the near term despite sustainability pressure, though incremental share shifts at the margin are real.

macroDrivers.title: Emerging-market household/personal-care penetration
macroDrivers.body: SLES demand growth is structurally tied to rising per-capita shampoo/detergent consumption in South/Southeast Asia, Africa, and Latin America — a genuine multi-decade volume driver distinct from mature-market cyclicality.

macroDrivers.title: Sulfate-free reformulation trend (mature markets)
macroDrivers.body: In North America and parts of Europe, "sulfate-free" positioning is a real, ongoing premium-segment reformulation trend away from SLES specifically — a structural headwind in mature markets even as emerging-market volume grows.

substitution.title: Sulfate-free alternatives (APG, sulfosuccinates, glutamates)
substitution.body: Alkyl polyglucosides and amino-acid-based surfactants are real, commercially available alternatives already used in "sulfate-free" formulations — a genuine and growing substitution path in premium personal care, though at a real cost premium and with different foam/formulation characteristics.

macroDrivers.title: Emerging-market household/personal-care penetration
macroDrivers.body: Same structural emerging-market volume driver as the 2EO grade.

substitution.title: Sulfate-free alternatives (APG, sulfosuccinates, glutamates)
substitution.body: Same sulfate-free substitution dynamic as the 2EO grade applies here.

macroDrivers.title: Toothpaste and HI&I cleaning demand growth
macroDrivers.body: SLS demand tracks broad-based oral care and household cleaning growth in emerging markets, alongside a genuine, ongoing "SLS-free" reformulation trend in premium toothpaste specifically (sensitivity/irritation positioning).

substitution.title: Milder anionic/amphoteric alternatives (sulfosuccinates, betaines)
substitution.body: Real substitution already occurring in premium/sensitive-skin formulations, though SLS retains a strong cost and foam-performance advantage for mainstream mass-market products.

macroDrivers.title: Toothpaste and HI&I cleaning demand growth
macroDrivers.body: Same structural demand driver as the paste form.

substitution.title: Milder anionic/amphoteric alternatives (sulfosuccinates, betaines)
substitution.body: Same substitution dynamic as the paste form.

macroDrivers.title: Mining and industrial water-treatment growth
macroDrivers.body: Fatty amine demand (flotation collectors, corrosion inhibitors) tracks mining sector activity and industrial water-treatment growth, both tied to broader industrial/infrastructure investment cycles.

substitution.title: Alternative quaternary/amine chemistries
substitution.body: Fatty amine performance in flotation and corrosion-inhibition applications is process-specific and well-established; genuine substitution is uncommon without a broader process redesign.

macroDrivers.title: Road construction and infrastructure investment
macroDrivers.body: Asphalt/bitumen additive demand (a major end use for this specific chain length) tracks global road construction and infrastructure investment cycles — a genuine, if somewhat cyclical, structural driver tied to government infrastructure spending.

substitution.title: Alternative asphalt adhesion promoters
substitution.body: Fatty amine-based adhesion promoters are well-established in asphalt formulation; genuine substitution is uncommon given established performance and specification history.

macroDrivers.title: "Clean label" and biodegradable surfactant demand growth
macroDrivers.body: APG is a direct beneficiary of the broader clean-label, readily-biodegradable surfactant trend in personal care and HI&I — a genuine, structural growth driver as brand owners reformulate toward "green" surfactant systems.

substitution.title: Other bio-based surfactants (sugar esters, glutamates)
substitution.body: APG occupies a fairly distinct performance/cost position among bio-based surfactants; genuine full substitution is limited, though it competes at the margin with other green-surfactant options for specific formulation slots.

macroDrivers.title: Mild/baby-care personal care segment growth
macroDrivers.body: Sulfosuccinate demand tracks the mild-surfactant/baby-care personal-care segment specifically, a smaller but genuinely growing niche as sensitivity-focused formulation continues to expand.

substitution.title: Other mild surfactants (glutamates, glucosides)
substitution.body: Sulfosuccinates occupy a specific foam/mildness performance niche; genuine substitution exists but each alternative has real formulation trade-offs, limiting wholesale switching.

macroDrivers.title: VOC regulation is a structural headwind
macroDrivers.body: Tightening VOC regulations in coatings (EU Solvents Emissions Directive, US state-level rules) are a genuine, ongoing structural headwind for solvent-borne toluene demand, even as waterborne coatings continue displacing solvent-borne systems long-term.

substitution.title: Waterborne coating systems
substitution.body: The multi-decade shift from solvent-borne to waterborne coatings is a real, ongoing structural substitution — not of toluene by another solvent, but of the whole solvent-based system by water-based technology.

macroDrivers.title: Paraxylene/polyester demand dominates the broader xylene market
macroDrivers.body: The much larger paraxylene-to-PTA-to-polyester demand pool (versus solvent-grade mixed xylenes) means broader textile/packaging demand trends, not paint/coatings trends, actually drive most global xylene market dynamics.

substitution.title: Waterborne coating systems
substitution.body: Same long-term solvent-to-waterborne coatings shift applies to xylene's solvent-grade use.

macroDrivers.title: Tied to phenol/BPA/MMA downstream demand cycles
macroDrivers.body: As a cumene-process co-product, acetone supply and cost are structurally linked to phenol, BPA, and MMA demand cycles (construction, automotive, electronics) rather than standalone acetone demand — a real, indirect macro linkage.

substitution.title: Alternative fast-drying solvents (MEK, IPA)
substitution.body: Genuine substitution exists at the margin for specific cleaning/degreasing applications, but acetone's low cost (co-product economics) makes wholesale switching uncommon.

macroDrivers.title: Biofuel policy linkage via shared feedstock/production base
macroDrivers.body: Industrial ethanol shares production infrastructure and corn/sugar feedstock with fuel ethanol, linking its cost and availability to biofuel policy and agricultural commodity cycles — a real, structural connection.

substitution.title: Isopropanol (IPA) for some cleaning/extraction uses
substitution.body: Partial substitutability exists for general cleaning/extraction applications, but regulatory/labeling requirements (denatured alcohol specifications) limit full interchangeability in many uses.

macroDrivers.title: Hand sanitizer/disinfectant demand normalization
macroDrivers.body: Demand structurally increased post-2020 and has partially normalized since — the multi-year trend is toward a "new normal" baseline above pre-2020 levels, not a return to pre-pandemic demand, as hygiene habits have durably shifted in some markets.

substitution.title: Isopropanol-based disinfectant formulations
substitution.body: IPA-based sanitizers are a genuine alternative already in wide use; the choice is often formulation/regulatory-driven rather than a pure substitution decision.

macroDrivers.title: Semiconductor/electronics manufacturing growth
macroDrivers.body: High-purity IPA demand for electronics cleaning tracks the structural, multi-year growth in global semiconductor fabrication capacity — a genuine long-term volume driver distinct from the more cyclical disinfectant-demand story.

substitution.title: Ethanol-based disinfectant formulations
substitution.body: Partial substitutability for general disinfectant use, but electronics-grade cleaning applications have no comparable low-residue alternative at similar cost.

macroDrivers.title: VOC regulation is a structural headwind
macroDrivers.body: Same solvent-borne-to-waterborne coatings structural shift applies to MEK as to toluene/xylene, given coatings is MEK's dominant application.

substitution.title: Alternative ketone/ester solvents
substitution.body: Some substitution exists at the margin, but MEK's specific evaporation-rate/solvency balance is well-established in coatings formulation, limiting wholesale switching.

macroDrivers.title: Personal care conditioning product growth
macroDrivers.body: Demand tracks broad-based shampoo/conditioner market growth in emerging markets — a stable, multi-year structural driver.

substitution.title: Cationic guar (GHPTC) and other conditioning polymers
substitution.body: Cationic guar derivatives offer a genuine, commercially established alternative conditioning mechanism, already used interchangeably by formulators depending on desired sensory profile — real substitution optionality exists.

macroDrivers.title: Automotive lightweighting and EV growth
macroDrivers.body: PA12's use in fuel/brake lines and flexible tubing benefits from the broader automotive lightweighting trend; EV-specific growth is more mixed since fuel lines are internal-combustion-specific, but flexible tubing and 3D-printing applications benefit from EV/lightweight-vehicle design trends generally.

substitution.title: Bio-based PA11 (castor-oil-derived)
substitution.body: PA11 (Arkema Rilsan) is a genuine, commercially available bio-based alternative with similar properties, already used interchangeably in some automotive/oil&gas applications — a real substitution option for buyers prioritizing renewable content.

macroDrivers.title: Building insulation demand tied to energy-efficiency regulation
macroDrivers.body: Rigid PU foam insulation demand is structurally supported by tightening building energy-efficiency codes globally — a genuine, regulation-driven multi-year growth driver, not just a construction-cycle story.

macroDrivers.title: Appliance efficiency standards
macroDrivers.body: Refrigerator/freezer insulation demand benefits similarly from tightening appliance energy-efficiency standards worldwide.

substitution.title: Non-isocyanate polyurethane (NIPU) technology
substitution.body: NIPU chemistry exists at lab/pilot scale as a genuine long-term alternative avoiding isocyanate handling/toxicity concerns, but remains far from commercial cost-competitiveness at scale — a real but distant substitution risk, not a near-term one.

macroDrivers.title: Footwear and elastomer demand growth
macroDrivers.body: Demand tracks global footwear production and TPU/cast-elastomer growth, both tied to consumer goods manufacturing trends, increasingly concentrated in Asia.

substitution.title: Non-isocyanate polyurethane (NIPU) technology
substitution.body: Same distant, pre-commercial NIPU substitution risk as polymeric MDI.

macroDrivers.title: Furniture and bedding demand growth
macroDrivers.body: Flexible foam demand tracks furniture/bedding consumption growth, structurally tied to housing formation rates and consumer discretionary spending in furnishing.

substitution.title: MDI-based flexible foam systems
substitution.body: Some flexible foam formulations can be reformulated around MDI instead of TDI — a genuine, real substitution path already used in some regions/applications, driven partly by TDI's stricter occupational exposure handling requirements.

macroDrivers.title: "Scent-boosting" laundry/fabric care product growth
macroDrivers.body: Long-lasting fragrance microcapsule demand tracks the genuine, ongoing premiumization trend in laundry care (scent boosters, fabric softener positioning) — a real, growing category.

substitution.title: Alternative encapsulation technologies (cyclodextrin, biopolymer)
substitution.body: Growing regulatory and consumer scrutiny of melamine-formaldehyde microplastics is a genuine driver toward biopolymer-based encapsulation alternatives — an active, real substitution trend, not just theoretical.

macroDrivers.title: Aerospace lightweighting and metal replacement
macroDrivers.body: PEEK's core value proposition — replacing metal in weight-sensitive, high-performance applications — is structurally supported by continued aerospace lightweighting trends and growing semiconductor/medical device demand.

macroDrivers.title: Aging population driving medical implant demand
macroDrivers.body: PEEK spinal implants and medical devices benefit directly from aging-population-driven growth in orthopedic and spinal procedures globally — a genuine, demographic-linked structural driver.

substitution.title: PEKK and other PAEK-family polymers
substitution.body: PEKK (Arkema Kepstan) offers similar performance and is a genuine alternative within the same broader polymer family, though Victrex's scale/cost advantage in standard PEEK limits real-world switching for most applications.

macroDrivers.title: Battery/EV growth is a major new demand driver
macroDrivers.body: PVDF's role as a lithium-ion battery electrode binder ties it directly to the structural, multi-decade EV and grid-storage battery growth trend — genuinely one of the strongest volume growth drivers in this entire database.

substitution.title: PFAS regulatory scrutiny is a real, active risk
substitution.body: PVDF is a fluoropolymer under increasing regulatory scrutiny as part of the broader EU PFAS restriction proposal — this is a genuine, live regulatory risk (not just a substitution risk) that could affect long-term availability and cost, worth monitoring closely given the size of the battery-binder growth opportunity riding on this same chemistry.

substitution.title: Alternative battery binders (aqueous/water-based binders)
substitution.body: Water-based binder alternatives (e.g., CMC/SBR systems) are a genuine, active area of battery R&D specifically to avoid PVDF/NMP processing — a real, credible substitution path being actively pursued by some battery makers.

macroDrivers.title: Personal care conditioning demand growth
macroDrivers.body: Tracks broad-based shampoo/conditioner market growth, similar to other conditioning polymers.

substitution.title: Natural oils and silicone alternatives (clean beauty trend)
substitution.body: The "silicone-free" clean-beauty positioning is a genuine, active reformulation trend in premium personal care, driving real substitution toward plant oils and alternative conditioning polymers in that specific segment.

macroDrivers.title: Industrial manufacturing and textile processing growth
macroDrivers.body: Tracks broader industrial manufacturing and textile production activity, particularly in Asia.

substitution.title: Alternative release agents and softeners
substitution.body: Silicone emulsions have well-established performance advantages in mold release and textile softening; genuine substitution is limited without accepting a real performance trade-off.

macroDrivers.title: LSR and specialty elastomer demand growth
macroDrivers.body: Growth in liquid silicone rubber applications (medical devices, automotive, consumer goods) is a genuine structural driver, particularly medical-grade LSR tied to aging-population healthcare demand.

substitution.title: Alternative elastomer chemistries (TPU, EPDM)
substitution.body: Silicone's unique temperature-range and biocompatibility performance limits genuine substitution in most high-value LSR applications.

macroDrivers.title: Broad industrial and cosmetic demand base
macroDrivers.body: Demand is diversified across many industrial and cosmetic uses, providing structural stability rather than a single strong growth vector.

substitution.title: Natural oils (cosmetic use) and alternative lubricants (industrial use)
substitution.body: Real substitution pressure exists in the cosmetic-use segment from the clean-beauty trend; industrial lubricant uses face less substitution pressure given silicone's specific performance advantages.

macroDrivers.title: Construction and glazing sealant demand
macroDrivers.body: Tracks construction activity broadly, with a structural tailwind from increasingly stringent building envelope/energy-efficiency sealing requirements.

substitution.title: Polyurethane and hybrid polymer sealants
substitution.body: Genuine alternative sealant chemistries exist and compete at the margin, but silicone's specific weathering/flexibility performance is well-established in glazing applications, limiting wholesale switching.

macroDrivers.title: Aerospace/defense and electronics growth
macroDrivers.body: Growth in electronics potting/encapsulation applications tracks broader electronics manufacturing growth, with aerospace/defense-grade applications tied to that sector's own investment cycle.

substitution.title: Epoxy potting compounds
substitution.body: Epoxy is a genuine alternative for some potting/encapsulation applications, but RTV-2's specific flexibility and low-shrinkage properties are often the reason it was selected, limiting real-world substitution.

macroDrivers.title: PU foam demand growth (see MDI/TDI cards)
macroDrivers.body: Directly tied to the same rigid/flexible PU foam demand drivers (building insulation, furniture/bedding) discussed on the MDI and TDI cards, since silicone surfactants are functionally essential to PU foam formation.

substitution.title: No credible non-silicone alternative for PU foam stabilization
substitution.body: This is a functionally non-substitutable input for essentially all PU foam production — genuine substitution risk is very low, distinct from most other products in this database.

macroDrivers.title: Emerging-market diaper penetration + aging-population incontinence demand
macroDrivers.body: Two distinct, both genuinely strong demographic drivers: rising disposable-diaper penetration in emerging markets (still well below developed-market levels) and aging-population-driven growth in adult incontinence products in developed markets — a rare case of two structural tailwinds pulling the same direction.

substitution.title: Cellulose-based absorbent alternatives
substitution.body: SAP's absorption-per-gram performance is far superior to cellulose/fluff pulp alone; genuine wholesale substitution is very unlikely given the core performance gap.

macroDrivers.title: Water scarcity and climate-driven agricultural adaptation
macroDrivers.body: Growing water scarcity and more frequent drought conditions in major agricultural regions is a genuine, strengthening structural driver for water-retention soil amendments — this is the fastest-growing SAP application segment for real, climate-linked reasons.

substitution.title: Alternative soil amendments (biochar, hydrogels)
substitution.body: Biochar and other emerging soil-amendment technologies offer genuine, if less proven, alternative approaches to water retention — a real but still-developing substitution pathway.

macroDrivers.title: Waterborne coatings growth (see solvent cards)
macroDrivers.body: HEUR demand tracks the same structural solvent-to-waterborne coatings shift that creates headwinds for solvent demand — this is the direct beneficiary side of that same multi-decade trend.

substitution.title: ASE (alkali-swellable emulsion) thickeners
substitution.body: HEUR displaced ASE thickeners specifically because of superior flow/leveling performance; reverting to ASE would mean accepting a real performance downgrade, making this a low-probability substitution.

macroDrivers.title: Clean-label food and natural personal-care demand
macroDrivers.body: Xanthan gum benefits structurally from the "natural/clean-label" ingredient trend in both food and personal care, being a fermentation-derived (not synthetic) thickener.

substitution.title: Guar gum and other natural gums
substitution.body: Guar gum offers a genuine alternative in some food/industrial applications at different cost and performance points — real substitution optionality exists depending on the specific rheology profile needed.

macroDrivers.title: Construction dry-mix mortar growth
macroDrivers.body: HEC demand tracks construction activity broadly, particularly the growing use of pre-mixed/dry-mix mortar systems in urbanizing markets.

substitution.title: Other cellulose ethers (HPMC, MC)
substitution.body: Different cellulose ether types serve overlapping but distinct performance niches; genuine wholesale substitution across the category is limited by these performance differences.

macroDrivers.title: Clear-gel and premium cosmetic formulation growth
macroDrivers.body: Carbomer demand tracks premium cosmetic/personal-care formulation growth specifically (clear gels, hand sanitizers), a somewhat narrower but genuinely growing niche.

substitution.title: Alternative synthetic thickeners (acrylates copolymers)
substitution.body: Lubrizol's Carbopol brand retains real technical/brand preference in premium formulations; genuine substitution exists but full switching is less common given established formulation history.

macroDrivers.title: Personal care conditioning demand growth
macroDrivers.body: Tracks broad-based shampoo/conditioner market growth, similar to other conditioning polymers.

substitution.title: Polyquaternium-7 and other synthetic conditioning polymers
substitution.body: Real substitution optionality exists between cationic guar and synthetic conditioning polymers depending on desired sensory profile and "natural" positioning — an active formulation choice, not a one-way street.

macroDrivers.title: Automotive lightweighting and EV growth
macroDrivers.body: Glass-fiber-reinforced PA6 benefits from continued automotive lightweighting trends; EV-specific growth is more nuanced (fewer engine-bay parts, but growing use in battery enclosures and structural components).

substitution.title: PA66 and other engineering plastics
substitution.body: PA6 and PA66 are often substitutable depending on specific temperature/mechanical requirements, giving buyers genuine but modest switching flexibility within the nylon family.

macroDrivers.title: Data center and electronics growth
macroDrivers.body: Polycarbonate demand benefits structurally from data center buildout (equipment housings) and continued electronics/EV growth (headlamp lenses, interior components) — genuine, multi-year volume drivers.

substitution.title: PMMA (acrylic) for some optical/glazing applications
substitution.body: PMMA offers better optical clarity but inferior impact resistance; genuine substitution is application-specific and limited where PC's impact performance is the reason for selection.

macroDrivers.title: Water/gas infrastructure investment growth
macroDrivers.body: HDPE pipe demand benefits structurally from aging-infrastructure replacement programs and continued urbanization/water-infrastructure investment globally — a genuine, policy-supported multi-year driver distinct from packaging-cycle demand.

macroDrivers.title: Recycled content requirements
macroDrivers.body: Growing regulatory and brand-owner recycled-content requirements are a structural shift affecting packaging-grade HDPE sourcing specifically, distinct from pipe-grade demand.

substitution.title: PP for some packaging applications
substitution.body: Some overlap exists between HDPE and PP in rigid packaging, but distinct performance profiles (chemical resistance, flexibility) limit wholesale substitution.

macroDrivers.title: E-commerce packaging growth
macroDrivers.body: LDPE film demand benefits structurally from continued e-commerce growth (shipping film, mailers) — a genuine, ongoing multi-year volume driver.

macroDrivers.title: Single-use plastic regulation is a structural headwind
macroDrivers.body: Growing single-use plastic bans and restrictions in the EU and elsewhere are a genuine, active headwind for LDPE film applications specifically.

substitution.title: Bio-based and compostable film alternatives
substitution.body: PLA and other compostable film materials are a genuine, growing substitution path in some packaging applications, driven directly by the same regulatory pressure — a real, active trend rather than theoretical.

macroDrivers.title: Nonwovens/hygiene and medical demand growth
macroDrivers.body: PP nonwoven demand benefits from the same hygiene-product demographic drivers (diapers, adult incontinence) discussed for SAP, plus medical textile demand — genuine, multi-year structural growth.

substitution.title: HDPE for some rigid applications
substitution.body: Limited genuine overlap given PP's distinct fatigue-resistance (living hinge) properties important to many of its applications.

macroDrivers.title: Waterborne coatings growth (structural beneficiary)
macroDrivers.body: Acrylic resin is the primary beneficiary of the multi-decade solvent-to-waterborne coatings shift — a genuine, strong structural tailwind, mirroring the substitution risk faced by solvents and alkyd resins.

substitution.title: Alkyd and hybrid alkyd-acrylic systems
substitution.body: Given acrylic is already displacing alkyd (not the reverse), genuine substitution risk to acrylic itself is low; if anything acrylic is the substitute technology already winning share.

macroDrivers.title: Structural, multi-decade decline versus waterborne acrylic
macroDrivers.body: This is one of the few products in this database facing a genuine long-term structural decline rather than growth — alkyd resin has been losing share to waterborne acrylic coatings for decades, and that trend shows no sign of reversing.

substitution.title: Waterborne acrylic coating systems
substitution.body: This substitution is not a future risk — it is an ongoing, decades-long structural shift already well underway. Buyers of alkyd resin should expect continued volume decline and supplier consolidation, not price stability from a healthy growing market.

macroDrivers.title: Wind energy and composite demand growth
macroDrivers.body: Epoxy's role as the standard wind-turbine-blade composite matrix resin ties it to the structural, policy-supported growth in wind energy installation globally — a genuine, strong multi-year driver.

macroDrivers.title: Electronics growth (PCB substrate demand)
macroDrivers.body: Electronics manufacturing growth supports epoxy demand via PCB substrate and encapsulation applications.

substitution.title: Vinyl ester and polyester resins (composite applications)
substitution.body: Genuine alternatives exist for some composite applications at lower cost/performance, but epoxy's superior mechanical properties are usually the reason for selection in high-value applications (wind blades, aerospace), limiting real substitution there.

macroDrivers.title: Powder coating growth (VOC-free positioning)
macroDrivers.body: Solid epoxy resin for powder coatings benefits from the same VOC-regulation-driven shift away from solvent-borne coatings, since powder coating is inherently VOC-free.

substitution.title: Polyester powder coating resins
substitution.body: Genuine alternative exists for some powder coating applications, particularly where UV/weathering resistance matters more than epoxy's chemical resistance — real but application-specific substitution.

macroDrivers.title: Recycled content mandates (rPET) are reshaping the market
macroDrivers.body: Growing regulatory recycled-content mandates (EU, several US states) are structurally shifting bottle-grade PET sourcing toward rPET — a real, binding requirement in some jurisdictions, not just a brand preference.

substitution.title: Aluminum cans and glass (packaging format substitution)
substitution.body: Format-level substitution (can vs. bottle) happens at the brand-owner packaging-design level for reasons beyond material cost; genuine wholesale material substitution away from PET bottles is limited given PET's cost/weight/clarity advantages.

macroDrivers.title: Recycled fiber (rPET) brand commitments
macroDrivers.body: Major apparel brands' public rPET-content commitments are a genuine, binding structural driver linking apparel-brand sustainability targets directly to bottle recycling rates.

substitution.title: Natural fibers (cotton) and other synthetics (nylon)
substitution.body: Cost and performance advantages keep polyester dominant in most apparel categories; genuine wholesale substitution is limited despite some "natural fiber" premium-market preference.

macroDrivers.title: Single-use plastic and polystyrene-specific bans
macroDrivers.body: Polystyrene faces some of the most direct regulatory targeting of any plastic (specific foodservice foam bans in many jurisdictions) — a genuine, active structural headwind distinct from general plastics regulation.

substitution.title: PP and PET for foodservice/packaging applications
substitution.body: Real, active substitution already occurring in foodservice packaging specifically driven by the regulatory bans — not a theoretical future risk.

macroDrivers.title: Construction and infrastructure investment growth
macroDrivers.body: PVC pipe/profile demand tracks construction and water-infrastructure investment globally — a genuine, stable multi-year driver, particularly in urbanizing emerging markets.

substitution.title: HDPE and PP pipe for some applications
substitution.body: Genuine overlap exists in some pipe applications, but PVC's cost advantage in pressure pipe applications limits wholesale substitution.

macroDrivers.title: Universal plastics/rubber production growth
macroDrivers.body: As an essentially universal plastics/rubber stabilizer, demand tracks broad global plastics production growth rather than any single end-market — a stable, diversified structural driver.

substitution.title: Alternative antioxidant chemistries (phosphites, thioesters)
substitution.body: Antioxidant packages are typically formulated with complementary chemistries rather than single substitutes; genuine wholesale substitution of hindered phenols specifically is uncommon given established performance and cost.

macroDrivers.title: Composite/wind energy growth (curing agent demand)
macroDrivers.body: Demand benefits from the same wind-energy and composite-manufacturing growth trends driving epoxy/vinyl-ester demand.

substitution.title: Alternative organic peroxide initiators
substitution.body: Different peroxide chemistries suit different cure-temperature profiles; genuine substitution exists within the category but is process-specific, not a simple drop-in swap.

macroDrivers.title: Grid infrastructure investment (XLPE cable demand)
macroDrivers.body: DTBP demand for XLPE cable crosslinking benefits from grid infrastructure investment and renewable energy transmission buildout globally — a genuine, policy-supported structural driver.

substitution.title: Alternative high-temperature peroxide crosslinkers
substitution.body: Genuine substitution exists within the peroxide category, but is process-temperature-specific.

macroDrivers.title: Water treatment and green chemistry demand growth
macroDrivers.body: H2O2 benefits structurally from its position as an environmentally-preferred oxidant (decomposes to water/oxygen) amid broader industrial decarbonization and green-chemistry trends, alongside steady pulp/paper and water-treatment demand.

substitution.title: Chlorine-based oxidants/bleaches
substitution.body: H2O2's environmental profile is generally preferred over chlorine-based alternatives; genuine substitution risk runs the other direction (H2O2 displacing chlorine), not away from H2O2.

macroDrivers.title: HPPO (propylene oxide) process growth
macroDrivers.body: The HPPO route to propylene oxide is a genuinely growing, more environmentally favorable process technology versus older chlorohydrin routes, providing a structural demand tailwind for concentrated H2O2 specifically.

substitution.title: Chlorine-based oxidants
substitution.body: Same dynamic as the 35% grade — substitution risk runs toward H2O2, not away from it.

macroDrivers.title: Semiconductor manufacturing capacity growth
macroDrivers.body: Directly tied to the structural, multi-year growth in global semiconductor fabrication capacity — a genuine strong volume driver, and a distinctly different demand story from the industrial-grade H2O2 cards.

substitution.title: No credible lower-purity substitute for wafer cleaning
substitution.body: Semiconductor fabs require this exact purity specification; genuine substitution risk is essentially nil for this specific application.

macroDrivers.title: Flexible PVC demand growth (construction, cable)
macroDrivers.body: Tracks flexible PVC demand broadly (flooring, cable insulation, automotive interiors), tied to construction and automotive production activity.

macroDrivers.title: Ongoing phthalate regulatory scrutiny is a genuine structural risk
macroDrivers.body: Continued regulatory review of phthalates generally (beyond the existing toys/childcare restriction) is a real, live risk that could affect long-term demand and require reformulation — worth monitoring rather than assuming current regulatory status is permanent.

substitution.title: Non-phthalate plasticizers (DINCH, bio-based citrates)
substitution.body: Genuine, commercially available non-phthalate alternatives already exist and are gaining share in sensitive applications (toys, medical, food contact) — a real, active substitution trend distinct from a theoretical future risk.

macroDrivers.title: Sun protection awareness and skin cancer prevention campaigns
macroDrivers.body: Growing skin-cancer awareness and dermatological sun-protection recommendations support structural growth in daily-wear SPF product usage globally — a genuine, health-driven multi-year demand trend.

substitution.title: Mineral UV filters (TiO2, ZnO) and newer organic filters
substitution.body: Mineral filters and newer-generation organic filters (Tinosorb, etc.) are genuine, commercially established alternatives already used in reef-safe and sensitive-skin formulations — real substitution optionality exists and is actively used by formulators.

macroDrivers.title: Construction and infrastructure investment growth
macroDrivers.body: Colored concrete/paver demand tracks construction activity broadly, particularly in urbanizing markets with growing decorative/architectural concrete use.

substitution.title: Organic black pigments (carbon black)
substitution.body: Carbon black offers different performance (less weather-stable in some formulations); genuine substitution is limited where iron oxide's specific durability is required.

macroDrivers.title: Construction and infrastructure investment growth
macroDrivers.body: Same construction-driven demand pattern as black iron oxide.

substitution.title: Organic red pigments
substitution.body: Organic reds offer brighter shades at higher cost and lower weather-stability; genuine substitution is limited for exterior/construction applications specifically.

macroDrivers.title: Construction and infrastructure investment growth
macroDrivers.body: Same construction-driven demand pattern as other iron oxide colors.

substitution.title: Organic yellow pigments
substitution.body: Same dynamic as red — organic alternatives offer brighter shade at the cost of weather-durability.

macroDrivers.title: Automotive and industrial coatings demand growth
macroDrivers.body: Tracks automotive production and industrial coatings demand broadly.

substitution.title: Ultramarine blue and other inorganic blues
substitution.body: Inorganic blues offer lower cost but inferior brightness/tinting strength; genuine substitution is limited where phthalocyanine blue's specific brilliance is required.

macroDrivers.title: Tire/vehicle production is the dominant driver — EV transition is nuanced
macroDrivers.body: As primarily a tire-reinforcement material, demand tracks global vehicle production and tire replacement cycles; EVs (heavier, higher-torque) generally require more robust tires, a modest structural positive, while battery-electrode conductive-additive use is a smaller but genuinely growing new demand vector.

substitution.title: Silica (in tire tread formulations)
substitution.body: Silica-reinforced "green tire" formulations are a genuine, already-significant substitution trend in tire tread specifically (improving rolling resistance/fuel economy), actively reducing carbon black's share of the tire reinforcement market — a real, ongoing shift, not theoretical.

macroDrivers.title: Tire/vehicle production growth
macroDrivers.body: As a rubber vulcanization activator, demand tracks tire and rubber goods production similarly to carbon black.

substitution.title: Alternative vulcanization activators
substitution.body: Zinc oxide's vulcanization performance is well-established; genuine substitution is uncommon given cost and established formulation history.

macroDrivers.title: Non-halogenated flame retardant shift
macroDrivers.body: Structural, regulation-driven shift away from halogenated flame retardants toward phosphorus-based chemistry is a genuine, ongoing multi-year tailwind for this product category specifically.

substitution.title: Alternative phosphorus flame retardants
substitution.body: Substitution exists within the broader phosphorus flame retardant family depending on specific application requirements, but the overall category trend favors this chemistry class, not away from it.

macroDrivers.title: Industrial water treatment and oilfield activity
macroDrivers.body: Demand tracks industrial cooling water treatment broadly and oilfield water management specifically, tied to industrial activity and oil & gas production levels.

substitution.title: HEDP and other phosphonates
substitution.body: Genuine substitution exists within the phosphonate family depending on specific scale/corrosion requirements (see the direct comparison already noted on this card), but wholesale movement away from phosphonates generally is limited.

macroDrivers.title: Industrial water treatment demand + biodegradability preference
macroDrivers.body: Same industrial water treatment demand driver as ATMP, with an added structural tailwind from HEDP's relatively better biodegradability profile amid tightening environmental discharge regulations.

substitution.title: ATMP and other phosphonates
substitution.body: Genuine substitution exists within the phosphonate family, with the choice typically driven by specific technical requirements rather than cost alone.

macroDrivers.title: Global tire production and vehicle fleet growth
macroDrivers.body: Tracks global tire production, itself tied to vehicle fleet growth in emerging markets and replacement-tire demand in mature markets — a stable, broad-based structural driver.

substitution.title: Natural rubber blending ratio adjustments
substitution.body: Tire formulators can shift BR/natural-rubber/SBR ratios at the margin in response to relative pricing, but wholesale substitution away from BR's specific abrasion-resistance role is uncommon.

macroDrivers.title: EV-driven "green tire" (low rolling resistance) growth
macroDrivers.body: S-SBR specifically benefits from a genuine structural tailwind: EV range-anxiety and fuel-efficiency regulation are both driving demand toward silica/S-SBR "green tire" formulations over conventional carbon-black/E-SBR systems.

substitution.title: Natural rubber and BR blending adjustments
substitution.body: Similar to BR, formulators adjust blend ratios at the margin, but SBR's role (especially S-SBR in green tires) is increasingly specified rather than substitutable.

macroDrivers.title: Automotive and industrial machinery production growth
macroDrivers.body: Tracks automotive and industrial equipment production, tied to fuel-system and hydraulic-seal demand specifically — a stable industrial-cycle-linked driver.

substitution.title: HNBR and fluoroelastomers (FKM) for demanding applications
substitution.body: Higher-performance alternatives exist for more demanding chemical/temperature environments, but at a real cost premium — genuine substitution is application-specific, not wholesale.

macroDrivers.title: Construction (roofing) and automotive growth
macroDrivers.body: Two distinct growth vectors: EPDM roofing membrane demand tracks commercial construction/re-roofing activity, while automotive sealing demand tracks vehicle production — both genuine, ongoing structural drivers, reinforced by real recent producer capacity investments.

substitution.title: TPO roofing membranes (construction use)
substitution.body: TPO (thermoplastic polyolefin) roofing has been gaining share against EPDM in commercial roofing specifically over the past decade — a genuine, active substitution trend in that application, distinct from EPDM's automotive sealing use where it remains dominant.

macroDrivers.title: Marine/recreational and industrial demand diversification
macroDrivers.body: Demand is diversified across wetsuits/marine, industrial gaskets, and cable jacketing, providing structural stability rather than one dominant growth vector.

substitution.title: EPDM and other synthetic rubbers for some seal/gasket uses
substitution.body: Some overlap exists in general-purpose sealing applications, but neoprene's specific chemical/weathering balance is well-established, limiting wholesale substitution.

macroDrivers.title: Multigrade oil demand + fuel-economy regulation
macroDrivers.body: Tightening vehicle fuel-economy and emissions standards are driving formulation toward lower-viscosity, higher-VI oils — a genuine structural driver for VI improver demand generally.

substitution.title: PMA-type VI improvers or PAO base stocks
substitution.body: Both are genuine, commercially available alternatives already used to avoid OCP's shear-stability limitation — real substitution optionality actively used by formulators, not theoretical.

macroDrivers.title: Multigrade oil demand + fuel-economy regulation
macroDrivers.body: Same structural driver as OCP-type VI improvers.

substitution.title: OCP-type VI improvers or PAO base stocks
substitution.body: Same substitution optionality as OCP, in the other direction — formulators choose based on specific low-temperature vs. shear-stability priorities.

macroDrivers.title: Emissions-catalyst compatibility is a structural constraint on growth
macroDrivers.body: Modern engine oil specifications increasingly limit zinc/phosphorus content to protect emissions catalysts — a genuine, ongoing regulatory constraint that caps (rather than grows) ZDDP's role in newer formulations, even as the vehicle fleet itself grows.

substitution.title: Ashless (zinc-free) antiwear additives
substitution.body: Ashless antiwear chemistry is a genuine, actively developing alternative specifically to meet tightening emissions-catalyst compatibility requirements — a real, regulation-driven substitution trend already underway in some specification tiers.

macroDrivers.title: Structural decline as refining shifts to Group II/III
macroDrivers.body: Group I capacity has been structurally shrinking for years as global refining capacity investment favors Group II/III — a genuine, ongoing supply-side decline independent of demand.

substitution.title: Group II base oil
substitution.body: This is an active, ongoing structural substitution already well underway across the lubricant industry — Group I is being phased out as a base stock of choice, not facing a future risk of displacement.

macroDrivers.title: Mainstream automotive lubricant demand (now the dominant tier)
macroDrivers.body: Group II has become the dominant global base oil tier for mainstream lubricants — demand tracks the broad global vehicle fleet and lubricant replacement cycle.

substitution.title: Group III base oil (premium upgrade) or Group I (cost downgrade)
substitution.body: Some formulations can shift between adjacent base oil groups depending on performance/cost targets, but each grade serves a fairly distinct specification tier, limiting casual substitution.

macroDrivers.title: Full-synthetic engine oil market growth
macroDrivers.body: Growth in full-synthetic-labeled motor oil (itself driven by OEM specification requirements and consumer premiumization) is a genuine, ongoing structural driver for Group III specifically.

substitution.title: True PAO synthetic base stocks (premium upgrade)
substitution.body: PAO offers superior but more expensive performance; genuine substitution runs toward Group III (cost-down) more often than away from it, given Group III's favorable cost/performance/"synthetic" labeling position.

macroDrivers.title: Fuel-economy-focused low-viscosity oil formulation
macroDrivers.body: Tightening fuel-economy regulation is a genuine structural driver toward lower-viscosity, higher-performance synthetic formulations specifically.

substitution.title: Group III base oil (cost-down substitution)
substitution.body: Group III increasingly approaches PAO-like performance at lower cost — a genuine, active substitution pressure on PAO from below, not just a theoretical possibility.

macroDrivers.title: Industrial gear/compressor demand growth
macroDrivers.body: Tracks industrial equipment demand broadly, tied to manufacturing and industrial capital investment cycles.

substitution.title: Group III or ester-based synthetic lubricants
substitution.body: Genuine cost-down substitution pressure from Group III exists here too, similar to the lower-viscosity PAO grade.

macroDrivers.title: Electronics/semiconductor manufacturing growth
macroDrivers.body: High-purity argon demand for semiconductor manufacturing tracks the structural, multi-year global fab-capacity growth trend.

substitution.title: Nitrogen (for some non-arc-welding inert applications)
substitution.body: Nitrogen can substitute in some general inerting applications, but argon's specific properties are required for arc welding and true inert-atmosphere needs, limiting wholesale substitution.

macroDrivers.title: Petrochemical and food cold-chain growth
macroDrivers.body: Diversified demand across petrochemical inerting (largest use) and food cold-chain growth in emerging markets provides structural stability across multiple growth vectors.

substitution.title: Argon or CO2 for some specific inerting/freezing uses
substitution.body: Limited genuine substitution given nitrogen's cost advantage (78% of air) for most inerting/purging applications.

macroDrivers.title: Steel/metals production growth + decarbonization
macroDrivers.body: Oxygen demand tracks steel production broadly; emerging "green steel" and electric-arc-furnace transition trends may shift (not necessarily reduce) oxygen demand patterns as the industry decarbonizes.

substitution.title: No credible substitute for combustion/steelmaking oxygen
substitution.body: Industrial oxygen has no practical substitute for its core combustion-enhancement and steelmaking role.

macroDrivers.title: Global vehicle fleet growth + regulatory mandate lock-in
macroDrivers.body: As the regulatorily mandated standard for new-vehicle mobile AC in major markets, demand is structurally guaranteed to grow with global vehicle production — an unusually secure, regulation-locked-in demand driver.

substitution.title: CO2 (R-744) mobile AC systems
substitution.body: Some manufacturers (notably in the EU) use CO2-based mobile AC as an alternative ultra-low-GWP technology, but R-1234yf remains the dominant standard — a real but currently minority substitution path.

macroDrivers.title: Structural, regulation-driven decline
macroDrivers.body: This is a structurally declining product under active multi-jurisdiction phase-down — expect continued volume decline as the installed base ages out and quota allowances shrink, not future growth.

substitution.title: R-1234yf (new equipment) and R-450A/R-513A (retrofit blends)
substitution.body: This substitution is already substantially complete for new vehicles; remaining R-134a demand is almost entirely legacy service/retrofit, a declining pool by definition.

macroDrivers.title: Heat pump adoption and building electrification
macroDrivers.body: R-32's growing adoption is directly linked to the broader heat-pump and building-electrification trend (itself tied to decarbonization policy) — a genuine, strong structural growth driver as heat pumps displace gas heating in more markets.

substitution.title: R-454B and other next-generation lower-GWP blends
substitution.body: Some manufacturers are moving toward even-lower-GWP blends beyond R-32; a real, live evolution rather than a stable end-state — R-32 itself may face its own future displacement.

macroDrivers.title: Structural, regulation-driven decline
macroDrivers.body: Same dynamic as R-134a — active phase-down means declining volume, not growth, for the foreseeable future.

substitution.title: R-32 and R-454B (new equipment)
substitution.body: Substitution is already substantially complete for new equipment across major manufacturers; remaining demand is service/retrofit for the existing installed base.

macroDrivers.title: CCUS and decarbonization policy is a genuinely new demand vector
macroDrivers.body: Beyond traditional industrial/food-grade use, carbon capture utilization and storage represents a genuinely new, policy-supported demand pool for CO2 as a captured/utilized molecule — a real structural shift in how this commodity is valued, not just traditional industrial-gas demand growth.

substitution.title: Nitrogen or other gases for some non-beverage applications
substitution.body: CO2's specific properties (beverage carbonation, dry ice, EOR) are generally not substitutable at reasonable cost.

macroDrivers.title: Green hydrogen transition — a long-term risk to this SMR-route card specifically
macroDrivers.body: The broader hydrogen economy is growing, but this card specifically tracks conventional SMR ("grey") hydrogen — a genuine, structural long-term risk exists as green (electrolysis-based) hydrogen scales and potentially displaces grey hydrogen in some applications, driven by decarbonization policy.

substitution.title: Green (electrolysis-based) hydrogen
substitution.body: Currently far more expensive than SMR hydrogen, but policy support (subsidies, carbon pricing) is a genuine, active force narrowing that gap over time — a real medium-term substitution risk worth monitoring, not an immediate one.

macroDrivers.title: Biodegradability regulation is a structural long-term headwind
macroDrivers.body: EDTA's poor biodegradability is under increasing environmental/eco-label scrutiny — a genuine, ongoing structural pressure favoring GLDA/MGDA over time, even though EDTA's cost advantage keeps it in wide use today.

substitution.title: GLDA and MGDA (biodegradable chelants)
substitution.body: Both are genuine, commercially available, readily-biodegradable alternatives already displacing EDTA in eco-labelled formulations — a real, active substitution trend, though EDTA retains a cost advantage in non-eco-labelled uses.

macroDrivers.title: Direct beneficiary of the EDTA-to-biodegradable-chelant shift
macroDrivers.body: GLDA is a direct beneficiary of the same regulatory/eco-label pressure that creates a headwind for EDTA — a genuine, strengthening structural tailwind.

substitution.title: MGDA (competing biodegradable chelant)
substitution.body: GLDA and MGDA compete with each other more than either competes against EDTA at this point; genuine but lateral substitution risk within the "green chelant" category.

macroDrivers.title: Direct beneficiary of the EDTA-to-biodegradable-chelant shift
macroDrivers.body: Same structural tailwind as GLDA.

substitution.title: GLDA (competing biodegradable chelant)
substitution.body: Same lateral competition dynamic as GLDA.

macroDrivers.title: Natural/green cleaning product demand growth
macroDrivers.body: Citric acid benefits from the broader "natural ingredient" cleaning-product trend, being a genuinely bio-based, readily biodegradable chelant/descaling agent.

substitution.title: EDTA or phosphonates for stronger chelation needs
substitution.body: Citric acid's mild chelation strength limits it to specific use cases; genuine substitution runs toward stronger chelants when performance requirements exceed citric acid's capability, not the reverse.

macroDrivers.title: Food and beverage consumption growth
macroDrivers.body: Tracks broad-based global food/beverage consumption growth, a stable and diversified structural driver.

substitution.title: Other food acids (malic, tartaric, lactic)
substitution.body: Genuine substitution exists for some flavor/formulation profiles, but citric acid's cost and flavor-neutrality advantages keep it dominant in most applications.

macroDrivers.title: Global food demand growth + resistance management needs
macroDrivers.body: Structural population and food-demand growth support continued fungicide use broadly; growing fungal resistance to older single-site chemistries actually supports continued/growing azoxystrobin demand as part of resistance-management rotation programs.

substitution.title: Other QoI fungicides and multi-site fungicides (mancozeb)
substitution.body: Resistance-management best practice actually requires ROTATION between different modes of action rather than full substitution — azoxystrobin's role in that rotation is structurally supported, not threatened, by resistance concerns.

macroDrivers.title: Resistance-management rotation demand
macroDrivers.body: As a multi-site fungicide, mancozeb's role in resistance-management rotation with single-site fungicides is structurally supported by the same growing resistance pressure — genuine, if unglamorous, demand stability.

substitution.title: Other multi-site fungicides (copper-based)
substitution.body: Copper-based fungicides offer some overlap but different application profiles; genuine substitution is limited given mancozeb's established broad-spectrum performance and cost position.

macroDrivers.title: Turf management market growth (golf, sports fields)
macroDrivers.body: Beyond row-crop agriculture, growth in professional turf management (golf courses, sports facilities) in emerging markets provides a distinct, additional demand vector.

substitution.title: Other systemic triazole fungicides
substitution.body: Genuine substitution exists within the triazole class depending on specific crop/disease combinations, but wholesale movement away from triazoles generally is limited.

macroDrivers.title: Active, divergent regulatory trajectory is the dominant "driver"
macroDrivers.body: Unlike most products in this database, chlorpyrifos's future is being determined more by regulatory decisions (EU/US restrictions vs. continued Indian registration) than by underlying agricultural demand growth — genuinely uncertain and jurisdiction-dependent, not a stable structural trend either way.

substitution.title: Pyrethroids (cypermethrin) and newer insecticide classes
substitution.body: In jurisdictions restricting chlorpyrifos, substitution to pyrethroids or newer chemistries is already actively happening, not a future possibility — genuine, high-probability displacement in regulated markets specifically.

macroDrivers.title: Emerging-market agricultural intensification + public health vector control
macroDrivers.body: Two distinct drivers: agricultural intensification in emerging markets, and structural public-health vector-control (mosquito) program demand — both genuine, ongoing volume supports.

substitution.title: Other pyrethroids and newer insecticide classes
substitution.body: Genuine substitution exists within the broader insecticide category depending on target pest/resistance profile, but pyrethroids' favorable toxicity profile keeps this class in wide use.

macroDrivers.title: Pollinator regulation is an active, ongoing structural headwind
macroDrivers.body: The EU's 2018 outdoor neonicotinoid ban is not an isolated event — pollinator-protection regulatory pressure continues to build in other jurisdictions, a genuine, ongoing structural risk to long-term demand in regulated markets, even as demand in non-restricted markets continues.

substitution.title: Newer insecticide classes (diamides, other modes of action)
substitution.body: Real, active substitution already occurring in EU-restricted markets specifically; a genuine and accelerating trend where neonicotinoid restrictions apply.

macroDrivers.title: No-till farming and herbicide-tolerant crop adoption growth
macroDrivers.body: Continued global adoption of no-till/conservation agriculture and herbicide-tolerant crop varieties in emerging markets supports structural volume growth, independent of the litigation-driven headline risk to the originator brand specifically.

substitution.title: Litigation and regulatory risk is a genuine, material headwind
substitution.body: Bayer's ongoing US litigation exposure is a real, material risk that has already affected market structure and could affect long-term availability/branding, independent of the underlying agronomic demand for the chemistry itself.

substitution.title: Alternative herbicide modes of action (for resistance management)
substitution.body: Growing glyphosate-resistant weed populations are a genuine, real driver toward tank-mixing or rotating with other herbicide modes of action — an active agronomic trend, not primarily a substitution-by-choice story.

macroDrivers.title: Global food demand and yield-intensification growth
macroDrivers.body: Structural population growth and the ongoing need for yield intensification on a roughly fixed global arable land base is one of the most durable, multi-decade demand drivers in this entire database.

substitution.title: Ammonium nitrate or other nitrogen sources (regional preference, not true substitution)
substitution.body: Regional agronomic preference exists (AN in parts of Europe, urea/UAN in North America), but this reflects farming practice rather than genuine substitutability — urea's cost-per-unit-nitrogen advantage keeps it dominant globally.

macroDrivers.title: Global food demand growth + finite phosphate rock reserves
macroDrivers.body: Same structural food-demand driver as urea, with an added long-term consideration: phosphate rock is a finite, geographically concentrated resource (Morocco holds the largest reserves), a genuine long-term supply-security factor distinct from demand growth itself.

substitution.title: MAP (monoammonium phosphate) or other phosphate fertilisers
substitution.body: Genuine substitution exists between phosphate fertiliser types depending on soil pH and nitrogen requirements, but all ultimately depend on the same finite phosphate rock resource.

macroDrivers.title: Global food demand growth, particularly quality-focused crops
macroDrivers.body: Potassium demand growth is particularly tied to fruit/vegetable and export-crop quality requirements in addition to general yield growth — a genuine, somewhat distinct demand driver from pure yield-focused nitrogen/phosphate demand.

substitution.title: Sulfate of potash (SOP) for chloride-sensitive crops
substitution.body: SOP is a genuine alternative for chloride-sensitive crops specifically (tobacco, some fruits), but at a real cost premium — MOP remains dominant for most bulk agricultural use.

macroDrivers.title: European agricultural demand + industrial explosives demand
macroDrivers.body: Two distinct demand pools — European fast-acting nitrogen fertiliser preference and industrial explosives (mining/quarrying) — both tied to their respective sector activity levels.

substitution.title: Urea or UAN (regional/agronomic preference)
substitution.body: Same regional-preference dynamic as urea — genuine but practice-driven, not purely cost-driven substitution.

macroDrivers.title: Upstream driver for the entire nitrogen fertiliser chain
macroDrivers.body: As the feedstock for urea, AN, and DAP, ammonia demand is structurally tied to the same global food-demand growth driver as all downstream nitrogen fertilisers — arguably the single most fundamental demand driver in this family.

macroDrivers.title: Green ammonia and hydrogen-carrier research
macroDrivers.body: Emerging interest in ammonia as a hydrogen carrier/marine fuel for decarbonization is a genuinely new, though still early-stage, demand vector distinct from traditional fertiliser use.

substitution.title: No credible substitute for nitrogen fertiliser feedstock
substitution.body: Ammonia's role as the Haber-Bosch-derived nitrogen source has no practical substitute at agricultural scale.

macroDrivers.title: Glass demand growth (construction, solar, auto)
macroDrivers.body: Soda ash's dominant end use (glass manufacturing) benefits from construction growth, solar panel glass demand growth specifically (a genuinely new and growing vector), and automotive glazing demand.

substitution.title: No credible substitute in glass manufacturing at scale
substitution.body: Soda ash's role as a glass-melting flux has no practical large-scale substitute.

macroDrivers.title: Broad industrial demand base, tied to chlorine co-production
macroDrivers.body: Caustic soda demand is structurally linked to chlorine demand (PVC, water treatment) as a co-product — its own growth is somewhat dependent on the health of the broader chlor-alkali complex rather than standalone demand.

substitution.title: Potassium hydroxide for some specialty applications
substitution.body: KOH is a genuine but higher-cost alternative used only where its specific properties are required; wholesale substitution is uncommon given caustic soda's cost advantage.

macroDrivers.title: Water/wastewater infrastructure investment growth
macroDrivers.body: Tracks municipal water treatment infrastructure investment and urbanization broadly — a stable, multi-year structural driver.

substitution.title: PAC (polyaluminum chloride)
substitution.body: PAC is a genuine, increasingly preferred alternative in many water treatment applications (faster floc formation, less sludge) — a real, ongoing substitution trend within the same broader aluminum-coagulant family, not away from aluminum-based coagulation generally.

macroDrivers.title: Water/wastewater infrastructure investment + cold-climate/DOC-removal preference
macroDrivers.body: Same water infrastructure driver as alum, reinforced by PAC's genuine performance advantages in cold-climate and DOC/microplastics-removal applications — a real, strengthening structural preference.

substitution.title: Traditional alum coagulant
substitution.body: Given PAC is already the more advanced/preferred technology in many applications, substitution risk runs toward PAC displacing alum, not the reverse.

macroDrivers.title: Challenging source-water treatment demand growth
macroDrivers.body: Same water infrastructure driver, specifically for higher-turbidity/challenging source waters requiring higher-basicity coagulants.

substitution.title: Standard 10% PAC or alum
substitution.body: Genuine substitution exists based on source-water characteristics; the choice is technical, not primarily cost-driven.

macroDrivers.title: Phosphorus-removal regulation is a genuine, strengthening driver
macroDrivers.body: Tightening nutrient-discharge regulations (e.g., UK AMP7/8 phosphorus limits) are a real, regulation-driven demand growth vector specifically for iron-based coagulants, evidenced by real recent producer capacity expansions.

substitution.title: Ferric chloride or aluminum-based coagulants
substitution.body: Genuine substitution exists between iron and aluminum coagulant families depending on specific water chemistry, but this is a technical choice, not a one-way structural shift.

macroDrivers.title: Water treatment demand + agricultural micronutrient demand
macroDrivers.body: Diversified demand across water treatment coagulation and agricultural iron-micronutrient supplementation provides structural stability across two distinct end markets.

substitution.title: Ferric salts (pre-oxidized) for direct coagulation use
substitution.body: Ferrous sulfate is often chosen specifically for its lower cost as a byproduct-derived material; genuine substitution exists but changes the cost profile meaningfully.

macroDrivers.title: Tied to chlor-alkali co-production economics
macroDrivers.body: A meaningful share of HCl supply is a byproduct of chlor-alkali and isocyanate production, linking its availability to those industries' operating rates rather than standalone HCl demand growth.

substitution.title: Sulfuric acid for some general acidification uses
substitution.body: Genuine substitution exists for general pH-adjustment applications, but HCl's specific role in oil-well acidizing and metal pickling is less substitutable.

macroDrivers.title: Phosphate fertiliser demand growth (direct link)
macroDrivers.body: A large share of global sulfuric acid demand is directly tied to phosphate fertiliser production (via the DAP card in this same family) — the same structural food-demand growth driver applies here, one step upstream.

substitution.title: No credible general-purpose substitute at comparable cost
substitution.body: Sulfuric acid's extremely low cost and versatility make wholesale substitution uncommon across its many industrial uses.

macroDrivers.title: Phosphate fertiliser demand growth + finite reserve dynamics
macroDrivers.body: Same structural food-demand and finite-phosphate-rock-reserve dynamics as the DAP card, one step upstream in the value chain.

substitution.title: No credible substitute for phosphate fertiliser feedstock
substitution.body: Phosphoric acid's role as the essential phosphate fertiliser intermediate has no practical substitute at scale.

macroDrivers.title: Water treatment and public health demand growth
macroDrivers.body: Tracks municipal water treatment and general disinfection demand, a stable, essential-use structural driver reinforced by ongoing public-health/hygiene awareness.

substitution.title: Alternative disinfectants (chlorine dioxide, UV, ozone)
substitution.body: Genuine alternatives exist in municipal water treatment specifically, but sodium hypochlorite's cost and simplicity keep it dominant for most applications.

macroDrivers.title: Upstream driver for the broader fermentation-chemical ecosystem
macroDrivers.body: As feedstock for xanthan gum, citric acid, and feed amino acids all tracked in this database, glucose syrup demand is structurally tied to growth across that entire fermentation-chemical ecosystem — a genuinely important, if indirect, aggregated driver.

substitution.title: Alternative sugar feedstocks (sucrose, cassava starch)
substitution.body: Genuine regional substitution exists depending on local agricultural feedstock economics, but corn-derived glucose syrup remains dominant in major production regions.

macroDrivers.title: Bioplastics (PLA) growth is a genuinely new demand vector
macroDrivers.body: Beyond traditional food/beverage use, PLA bioplastic demand growth is a real, structurally distinct new driver for lactic acid, tied to broader sustainable-packaging trends — genuinely additive to, not just a restatement of, food-sector demand.

substitution.title: Other food acids (citric, malic)
substitution.body: Genuine substitution exists for some food formulation profiles, but limited for the PLA/bioplastic use case where lactic acid is the specific required monomer.

macroDrivers.title: Water treatment and papermaking demand growth
macroDrivers.body: Same broad water-treatment and papermaking demand drivers as the other PAM ionic types.

substitution.title: Anionic or cationic PAM depending on application charge requirements
substitution.body: The choice of ionic type is application-specific (particle charge dependent), not a cost-driven substitution decision.

macroDrivers.title: Defense/security spending and ballistic protection demand
macroDrivers.body: Global defense and law-enforcement spending growth, alongside rising personal/vehicle armor demand in security-conscious markets, is a genuine, geopolitically-linked structural driver.

substitution.title: UHMWPE (ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene) fiber
substitution.body: UHMWPE fiber (e.g., Dyneema, Spectra) is a genuine, commercially established alternative in body armor and some ballistic applications, offering a real lighter-weight alternative already used by some manufacturers — active substitution optionality, not theoretical.

macroDrivers.title: Wind energy growth is a major structural driver
macroDrivers.body: Large-tow carbon fiber demand for wind turbine blade spar caps benefits directly from the structural, policy-supported growth in wind energy installation, particularly as turbines scale up in size.

macroDrivers.title: EV lightweighting demand
macroDrivers.body: Growing EV lightweighting needs (extending range by reducing weight) support continued automotive carbon fiber adoption, though cost remains a genuine barrier to mass-market penetration.

substitution.title: Glass fiber (cost-sensitive applications)
substitution.body: Glass fiber is a genuine, much lower-cost alternative already used where carbon fiber's specific strength-to-weight advantage isn't essential — real substitution already occurs at the margin based on application requirements.

macroDrivers.title: Marine and transportation demand + wind energy (secondary)
macroDrivers.body: Tracks boat/marine manufacturing and transportation composite demand; wind energy also uses E-glass in blade construction alongside or instead of carbon fiber depending on turbine size/design.

substitution.title: Carbon fiber for higher-performance applications
substitution.body: Substitution generally runs the other direction (carbon fiber for premium applications) given E-glass's cost advantage; genuine risk to E-glass itself is low.

macroDrivers.title: Wind energy and infrastructure growth
macroDrivers.body: Wind turbine blade reinforcement and infrastructure composite (rebar, structural profiles) demand both benefit from genuine, ongoing structural growth trends.

substitution.title: Carbon fiber for higher-performance applications
substitution.body: Same dynamic as chopped strand mat — E-glass's cost advantage limits genuine substitution risk to itself.

macroDrivers.title: Aerospace lightweighting + aging-population medical demand
macroDrivers.body: Same dual driver as the Specialty Polymers PEEK card — aerospace metal-replacement trends and aging-population-driven medical implant growth.

substitution.title: PEKK and other PAEK-family polymers
substitution.body: Same genuine but limited substitution dynamic as the Specialty Polymers PEEK card.

macroDrivers.title: Battery/EV growth is a major new demand driver
macroDrivers.body: Same strong battery-binder demand driver as the Specialty Polymers PVDF card.

substitution.title: Aqueous/water-based battery binders
substitution.body: Same genuine, actively-pursued substitution risk as the Specialty Polymers PVDF card, given shared PFAS regulatory scrutiny.

macroDrivers.title: Global meat/protein consumption growth
macroDrivers.body: Rising per-capita meat consumption in emerging markets (particularly poultry and swine) is one of the most durable, multi-decade structural demand drivers for feed amino acids generally.

macroDrivers.title: Precision nutrition / lower-crude-protein diet trend
macroDrivers.body: Growing adoption of "precision nutrition" (lower crude-protein diets supplemented with specific amino acids) is a genuine structural tailwind, since it directly increases reliance on amino acid supplementation like lysine rather than raw protein feed.
